checks.name: Canonical storage
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation canonical_storage::
checks.output: 3 tests pass. CanonicalSchedule (src/automation.rs:99) has exactly three variants -- Once{at}, Every{interval_ms}, Cron{expression,timezone} -- and no prose variant, so an unparsed expression has nowhere to be stored. 'every hour' resolves to Every{3_600_000} and 'Daily' to Cron{"0 0 * * *", "UTC"} case-insensitively; 'sometime tomorrow', 'when the build is green' and 'often' each return the typed category ambiguous_expression rather than a guess.

checks.name: Round-trip
checks.command: rustc --edition 2024 --extern automonique_protocol=rust/target/debug/libautomonique_protocol.rlib -L dependency=rust/target/debug/deps - -o <scratch>/probe2 (program calling CanonicalSchedule::parse on each schedule's own render()) && <scratch>/probe2
checks.output: Parsing a canonical rendering does not yield the schedule; it yields a refusal. The probe printed, for all three canonical forms: ROUNDTRIP FAIL rendered=once@1000 category=ambiguous_expression, ROUNDTRIP FAIL rendered=every@60000 category=ambiguous_expression, ROUNDTRIP FAIL rendered=cron@0 0 * * *@UTC category=ambiguous_expression. CanonicalSchedule::parse (src/automation.rs:126) matches four literal strings only ('every hour', 'hourly', 'every day', 'daily'); there is no reader for the render() format. The in-repo test canonical_storage::a_canonical_schedule_round_trips_through_its_rendering never calls parse -- it asserts only that render() is deterministic and that two different schedules render differently -- so the named property is untested as well as false. There is no DST fixture corpus and no timezone arithmetic anywhere in the module.

checks.name: Occurrence idempotency
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation occurrence_idempotency::
checks.output: 3 tests pass. OccurrenceKey::derive takes exactly the automation id and the canonical instant and returns the deterministic string "{id}@{millis}"; eight repeated derivations are equal, a different automation id or a different instant yields a different key, and the key carries no nonce, clock read or sequence number, so a replayed tick after failover derives the same key without coordination.

checks.name: Revision immutability
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation revision_immutability::
checks.output: 2 tests pass. AutomationRevision::edited returns a new value at revision+1 and leaves the receiver at its original revision (3 stays 3, the successor is 4); a stale expectation returns AutomationError::RevisionConflict{expected:3, offered:2} instead of overwriting. All fields are private with no setter.

checks.name: Scope authority
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation scope_authority:: ; grep -in 'approval' rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/automation.rs
checks.output: 3 tests pass on the refusal half: an effect in the declared list is permitted, 'deploy:production' outside it returns AutomationError::OutsideApprovedScope{effect}, and an automation with an empty list permits nothing. The other half is not modelled. The row requires an out-of-scope effect to be 'representable only as an approval request'; permit_unattended returns Result<(), AutomationError>, and grep for 'approval' in src/automation.rs matches only the error-variant doc text -- there is no ApprovalRequest value, no pending-approval type and no way to express the request that the refusal is supposed to become.

checks.name: Job parity
checks.output: No job type exists. The only match in either file is the word 'outbox' inside a doc comment on TriggerRoute::delivers_directly. There is no no-agent script job, no agent job and therefore no shared type path to prove they carry identical identity, sandbox and outbox obligations. The automation test binary has 19 tests in 8 modules (canonical_storage, occurrence_idempotency, revision_immutability, scope_authority, evidence_bound_completion, wait_resolution, fenced_claims, trigger_routes) and none for this row.

checks.name: Verdict closure
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation (full binary, all 19 test names enumerated)
checks.output: No test in the repository exercises this row. I enumerated every test name in the automation binary; none asserts that the verdict set is closed, that it is exhaustive over the five outcomes, or that every verdict carries evidence. GoalVerdict (src/automation.rs:305) does have exactly five variants and each carries a payload, but the task forbids inferring a pass from source, and the one structural oddity I can see -- Wait carries a WaitCondition rather than evidence -- is exactly the kind of thing a covering case per outcome would have to rule on. Recorded as unmeasured rather than passed.

checks.name: Evidence-bound completion
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation evidence_bound_completion:: ; rustc --edition 2024 --emit=metadata --extern automonique_protocol=... - <<< 'fn main(){ let v = GoalVerdict::Complete{ evidence: String::from("it looks done") }; }'
checks.output: The three in-repo tests pass: a narrative goal closes on prose, a goal requiring Artifact refuses prose with CompletionEvidenceMissing{required:"artifact"} and closes on the artifact, and the same holds for Tests and Receipt. But the row requires the deficient completion to 'fail to typecheck', and it does not: I compiled `GoalVerdict::Complete { evidence: String::from("it looks done") }` against the built rlib and rustc exited 0. GoalVerdict is a public enum with public variant fields, so the Goal::complete_with gate at src/automation.rs:390 is a runtime check that any caller can route around by constructing the verdict directly. Nothing bans that construction and no compile_fail case covers it -- src/automation.rs contains zero compile_fail blocks.

checks.name: Wait resolution
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation wait_resolution::
checks.output: 1 test passes over all three variants. WaitCondition (src/automation.rs:338) is Timer{until: EpochMillis}, Run{run_id}, ConnectorEvent{source_key} -- there is no free-text-label variant, so a wake cannot resolve from prose and the property the row names holds. Noted rather than counted against it: the row lists four durable kinds and the 'monitored pattern' kind has no variant, and the single test is a match arm over the three variants rather than a rejection case.

checks.name: Trigger routes
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation trigger_routes::
checks.output: 3 tests pass and cover four required arguments: verification method (Hmac/PublicKey/MutualTls), replay window, body ceiling and the direct-delivery flag, plus a rejection for an empty route id. TriggerRoute (src/automation.rs:454) has exactly five fields. The row also requires filters, destination and idempotency extraction to be required, and the contract body additionally requires path, tenant and service actor, allowed event types, header limits and the sandboxed transform or typed template. None of those eight exists as a field or an argument, so a route that declares no destination and no idempotency extraction is constructible. 'Direct delivery still carries destination authorization and receipts' is asserted only in a doc comment, since neither a destination nor a receipt is representable here.

checks.name: Fenced claims
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation fenced_claims::
checks.output: 1 test passes on the epoch half: BoardClaim carries an epoch, is_current(7) and is_current(6) hold for a claim at epoch 7, and is_current(8) is false, so a newer epoch fences an older claim out. The remaining two clauses have nothing to measure. There is no label type anywhere in src/automation.rs, so 'labels cannot serve as tenancy controls' is neither enforced nor testable, and there is no failure threshold, retry counter or blocked state, so 'failure thresholds block rather than retry unboundedly' is unimplemented.
